headline: Binary consequences of relation-liveness automata lower bounds
abstract: We give explicit fixed-binary-alphabet consequences of OpenAI’s two relation-liveness lower bounds. Encoding each relation on h points by its h² adjacency bits gives a language recognized by a one-way nondeterministic automaton with Nₕ=(3h³−h)/2+2 states. Every equivalent two-way deterministic automaton, and every two-way nondeterministic automaton for its full binary complement, requires 2^{Ω(h)}=2^{Ω(Nₕ^(1/3))} states. We specify all transition rules, including an exact sh²-state pullback for an s-state binary target. The binary language rejects incomplete blocks; a fooling set proves that its one-way nondeterministic state complexity is Θ(h³). The exponential obstructions are inherited from the two upstream theorems; binary adjacency coding is established machinery.
